item.title: Nearly 20 years after launch, ancient AMD Radeon HD 2000 and 3000 GPUs finally get a Linux fix for corrupted video playback
item.description:
AI summary: A newly accepted Linux kernel patch, slated for Linux 7.5, fixes a long-standing video corruption bug on AMD's R600-based Radeon HD 2000 and HD 3000 cards (RV610, RV620, RV630, RV635, RV670) during hardware-accelerated video playback when the GPU was also handling 3D or desktop drawing. The fix keeps UVD decoder buffers in VRAM for these chips, a behavior the driver already enforced for several other families, and it was verified only by the submitter on an iMac7,1 running Debian, so other hardware in the family still needs testing. For those following AMD, it shows that the open-source Linux driver support for very old Radeon hardware is still being maintained years after proprietary Windows support ended.

From Tom's Hardware: A new kernel contributor used AI to develop a patch for the drivers powering his nearly-20-year-old Radeon GPU.
